_comment: Classifies the 25 negative golden-set rows (empty Card IDs) into the two kinds
the PRD (§Evaluation) and DECISIONS-Explain-This.md score separately: true_gap
(no card exists for anything the sentence turns on) vs false_friend (a content
word IS a shelf card title/alias, but this sentence uses a different sense).
Method: mechanical, not eyeballed. For each row's sentence, normalise it
(lowercase, strip punctuation, collapse whitespace) the same way
explain/index.js's normalise() does, then look for any shelf card title or
alias appearing as a whole-token match — i.e. the exact word-boundary rule
explain/retrieve.js's lexicalLeg() uses, including its MIN_SURFACE_CHARS=3
floor (a 1-2 char surface, e.g. the alias 'ai', never counts as a match).
A row with at least one such hit is false_friend; a row with none is
true_gap. Checked against shelf/shelf-export.json, version shelf-1010-02e436fd8106.
This mechanical check is a proxy for 'different sense', not a semantic judge —
row 27 is a genuine edge case where the hit is arguably the SAME sense; see
its reason for why it's still filed here rather than as a true_gap.
2026-10-18: row 27 (NLP) moved to positive with Card IDs [nlp], as its own note recommended; rows 40-54 added from Sumit's real-world non-AI sentences, classified with the same mechanical rule.

rows.sentence: Young people should vote for younger representatives who have a skin-in-the-game for our country's future.
rows.reason: No content word (skin-in-the-game, representatives, vote, younger) matches any shelf card title or alias. Plain civics sentence; nothing on the shelf is even adjacent.

rows.sentence: After helping design and build our Horizon AI incubator last year, I'm excited to officially take on the role of AI Enablement Strategist!
rows.reason: "AI" is technically an alias of the artificialintelligence card, but at 2 characters it sits below the lexical leg's MIN_SURFACE_CHARS=3 floor (explain/retrieve.js) and never fires as a match. No other word hits. Filed as true_gap because the mechanical check the harness actually runs finds nothing — consistent with the gold explanation ("AI" here is a program name and job title, not the concept).

rows.sentence: You don't need to be an engineer, but you need to be technically credible enough to make good build-vs-buy decisions, spot architectural risks early, and earn respect from a strong engineering team.
rows.reason: "spot" (as in "spot architectural risks") is a whole-word match against the alias "spot" on the spotinstances card (Spot instances — interruptible cloud compute). The sentence uses "spot" as an ordinary verb (notice), not the cloud-pricing sense.

rows.sentence: The Joker in Batman universe is portrayed as an agent of chaos, mastermind but also as a person who spoils people for fun.
rows.reason: "agent" matches the alias "agent" on the agents card. This is the PRD's own worked example of a false friend ("agent of chaos" — the everyday sense, not an AI agent).

rows.sentence: Poshak alerted me of his father's death.
rows.reason: No content word matches any shelf card title or alias. Personal message, no AI content at all.

rows.sentence: In sexual harassment and misconduct cases, establishing whether consent was present, absent, or legally invalid is the fundamental standard for determining accountability, distinguishing unwelcome behavior from mutual interaction.
rows.reason: "consent" matches the consent card (data/informed consent in AI) and "accountability" matches the accountability card. This is the PRD's own worked example of a false friend (consent in the legal sense, not the AI-governance sense).

rows.sentence: What I saw on the weather dashboard was harrowing: the storm was traveling in the same direction.
rows.reason: "dashboard" matches the dashboards card (a UI pattern for monitoring model/agent metrics). The sentence uses it as an ordinary weather display, not the AI-monitoring sense.

rows.sentence: As a college dropout, he struggled to get a job.
rows.reason: "dropout" matches the dropout card (the regularization technique). This is the PRD's own worked example of a false friend (leaving college, not the ML regularizer).

rows.sentence: In chronology and periodization, an epoch or reference epoch is an instant in time chosen as the origin of a particular calendar era.
rows.reason: "epoch" matches the epoch card (one full pass over the training data). This is the PRD's own worked example of a false friend (the calendar-era sense, not the ML-training sense).

rows.sentence: His last five movies were all flops.
rows.reason: "flops" matches the flops card (floating point operations, a compute-cost unit). The sentence uses it as ordinary slang for failed films, not the FLOPs sense.

rows.sentence: The hospital’s HMIS solution consumes this information and generates a token number or queue number for the patients.
rows.reason: "token" matches the tokens card and "queue" the requestqueue card; the sentence means a hospital queue ticket. Added 2026-10-18 from Sumit's real-world sentences.

rows.sentence: In the 1960s and 1970s, anti-CIA activists occasionally revealed long lists of overseas intelligence agents to sabotage their activities.
rows.reason: "agents" matches the agents card; the sentence means intelligence agents (spies). Added 2026-10-18 from Sumit's real-world sentences.

rows.sentence: What happens if I just make the air gap bigger for 480 V in a vacuum chamber? You move the failure to a lower pressure instead of removing it.
rows.reason: "air gap" matches the airgap card; the sentence means the gap between electrical conductors. Added 2026-10-18 from Sumit's real-world sentences.

rows.sentence: Symptoms begin before age 12 and include fidgeting, difficulty paying attention and losing things.
rows.reason: "attention" matches the attention card; the sentence means a person paying attention. Added 2026-10-18 from Sumit's real-world sentences.

rows.sentence: Optimizing batch production in manufacturing is all about finding the right balance between batch size and efficiency.
rows.reason: "batch size" matches the batchsize card; the sentence means factory production batches. Added 2026-10-18 from Sumit's real-world sentences.

rows.sentence: The term "community capacity building" (CCB) began to be used in 1995 and since then became popular for example within the policy literature in the United Kingdom, particularly in the context of urban policy, regeneration and social development.
rows.reason: "capacity" matches the capacity card; the sentence means community capacity building in social policy. Added 2026-10-18 from Sumit's real-world sentences.

rows.sentence: Make a cup of tea, pour a glass of wine, get cosy, and pick a few of these conversation starters.
rows.reason: "conversation" matches the conversation card; the sentence means people talking. Added 2026-10-18 from Sumit's real-world sentences.

rows.sentence: The Digger and other biggest flops of the century: what an epic movie flop means for Tom Cruise and Hollywood.
rows.reason: "flops" matches the flops card; the sentence means films that failed. Added 2026-10-18 from Sumit's real-world sentences.

rows.sentence: Gemini lies between Taurus to the west and Cancer to the east, with Auriga and Lynx to the north, Monoceros and Canis Minor to the south, and Orion to the south-west.
rows.reason: "Gemini" matches the gemini card; the sentence means the constellation. Added 2026-10-18 from Sumit's real-world sentences.

rows.sentence: Writing the Ensemble Cast: A Screenwriter’s Guide to Balancing Multiple Characters.
rows.reason: "ensemble" matches the ensemble card; the sentence means an ensemble cast. Added 2026-10-18 from Sumit's real-world sentences.

rows.sentence: The Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 is India's primary umbrella legislation designed to protect and improve the environment and prevent hazards to human beings, plants, animals, and property.
rows.reason: "environment" matches the environment card; the sentence means the natural environment in law. Added 2026-10-18 from Sumit's real-world sentences.

rows.sentence: Effective goal scoring requires not just shooting ability but also intelligent movement off the ball.
rows.reason: "goal" matches the goal card; the sentence means scoring in football. Added 2026-10-18 from Sumit's real-world sentences.

rows.sentence: An axial color gradient (sometimes also called a linear color gradient) is specified by two points, and a color at each point.
rows.reason: "gradient" matches the gradient and checkpointing cards; the sentence means a color gradient. Added 2026-10-18 from Sumit's real-world sentences.

rows.sentence: The Trojans were Anatolian (Luwian) people from northwestern Anatolia (modern-day Turkey), rather than ethnic Greeks.
rows.reason: "Trojans" is the plural of the trojan card (a hidden backdoor in a model). The mechanical whole-token check misses it because retrieval has no plural handling ("trojans" != "trojan"), so it was first filed as true_gap; Sumit caught it. The sentence means the ancient people of Troy. Added 2026-10-18 from Sumit's real-world sentences.

rows.sentence: In some legal jurisdictions there may be a requirement that the accused disclose an alibi defence prior to the trial.
rows.reason: "alibi" matches the alibi card (ALiBi, a position-encoding method); the sentence means a legal alibi. Added 2026-10-18 from Sumit's real-world sentences.
